content: Tiaprofenic acid is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that belongs to the arylpropionic acid (profen) class. It is primarily used to manage pain, particularly pain associated with arthritis. The standard adult dosage is 300 mg taken twice daily. However, its use is not recommended in children. Tiaprofenic acid undergoes minimal metabolism in the liver, resulting in the formation of two inactive metabolites. The majority of the drug is excreted unchanged in the urine. In patients with renal disease, the excretion of the drug is impaired, necessitating cautious use in this population. Prolonged use of tiaprofeneic acid has been linked to a significantly increased risk of severe cystitis, occurring approximately 100 times more frequently compared to other NSAIDs. Consequently, it is contraindicated in patients with a history of cystitis or urinary tract infections. The drug was first reported for clinical use in France in 1975. It is marketed under the trade names Surgam, Surgamyl, and Tiaprofen, as well as in generic formulations. A sustained-release preparation of the drug is also available. Tiaprofenic acid is an isomer of suprofen.
